cards.method: Quantile regression (+ Growth-at-Risk, ABG)
cards.when: modelling the whole conditional distribution of an outcome given covariates (several tau); a lower-tail tau = Growth-at-Risk (ABG)
cards.when_not: only the mean effect -> OLS; a descriptive tail without covariates -> #65; nlrq/crq/rqss are out of scope; a very small n (rank-deficient)

alternatives.criterion: you want the FULL growth density + expected shortfall from the GaR quantiles (ABG step 2) — the natural next step
the mean effect suffices, homoskedasticity
a tail metric without covariates (descriptive)
a full posterior / non-crossing / a skew-t likelihood
a tail driven by volatility clustering

output_key_fields: coefficients: long-format tau/term/estimate/std_error/t_value/p_value (one block per tau)
quantiles: long-format row_id/tau/predicted; crossing/any_crossing = quantile-crossing flag+count
qr_slope_equality: statistic/ndf/ddf/p_value (a pseudo-F test of equal slopes across quantiles)
gar: row_id/gar/upside (gar=fitted risk_tau, upside=fitted 1-risk_tau); curve = the full curve
n = the complete rows remaining; n_total/n_dropped; h; risk_tau/upside_tau; the fitted-model handle
interpretation_traps: quantile crossing: fitted quantiles are non-monotone in tau — flagged and counted, not hidden; any_crossing=True -> suspect predictions
GaR h-lead: for h>0 the prediction y_{t+h}~x_t uses orig_last (x_T), NOT a stale x_{T-h}; gar = the GaR h steps ahead, not today
a tau outside (0,1) is blocked (rq accepted it for the WHOLE process)
risk_tau must be ONE of the fitted tau (otherwise stop)
se='boot' is the only stochastic option, so the generator is seeded before the summary; the simplex and interior-point solvers are deterministic
sources: Koenker & Bassett 1978 (Econometrica 46:33, regression quantiles)
Koenker & Bassett 1982 (Econometrica 50:43, slope-equality Wald test)
Koenker 2005 Quantile Regression, Cambridge U. Press
Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone 2019 (AER 109:1263, Vulnerable Growth / GaR)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (time-series GaR only: stationarity, +KPSS confirmatory with the opposite polarity)
qr_slope_equality (the across-quantile slope test: do the slopes differ across quantiles? -> it justifies Growth-at-Risk, and needs at least 2 tau)

cards.method: Value-at-Risk / Expected Shortfall / downside-risk / component-VaR
cards.when: downside-risk metrics for a return series: VaR/ES/CVaR, drawdown/semi-deviation/Sortino, skew/kurtosis, portfolio component-VaR (Euler)
cards.when_not: a conditional-on-covariates tail -> #64 GaR; a volatility-clustering tail -> GARCH; EVT/GPD/kernel/MC were excluded; the historical component (non-additive)

alternatives.criterion: no distributional assumption, large n (an ex-post empirical tail)
a small sample / RiskMetrics parametric, returns ~normal
skew/excess kurtosis — check cf_valid
a conditional-on-covariates tail
volatility clustering drives the tail

output_key_fields: var/es: long-format series/var (plus es/es_ge_var); p/method/clean/invert/cf_valid/na_count/sign_convention
sign_convention: invert=False (our default) -> a POSITIVE loss magnitude; invert=True -> a signed quantile
downside summary: matrix metric x series (StdDev/SemiDev/DownsideDev/maxDD/VaR/ES/skew/kurt/Sortino)
risk_component_var: portfolio_var scalar + contributions (series/contribution/pct_contribution)
es_ge_var: |ES|>=|VaR| per series (a check on magnitude, independent of invert)
interpretation_traps: sign convention: invert=False => a positive loss magnitude (VaR=0.029 is a 2.9% loss); NEVER assume the sign, read sign_convention
modified / Cornish-Fisher: non-finite, or |ES|<|VaR|, sets cf_valid=False (not silent); a gaussian or historical violation is a hard stop
component: gaussian/modified only (the historical component is NOT additive -> silently wrong); POST-GATE Euler additivity; a negative contribution = a diversifier
gaussian/modified VaR is UNCONDITIONAL (constant mu, sigma); not conditional/volatility-driven
SE=False is pinned -> no random draws (deterministic); skew/kurt give the tail shape (excess kurtosis>0 -> a gaussian VaR understates)
sources: Zangari 1996 (RiskMetrics Monitor, Cornish-Fisher / modified VaR)
Favre & Galeano 2002 (J. Alternative Investment 5, Mean-Modified VaR)
Boudt, Peterson & Croux 2008 (J. of Risk 11:79, downside risk decomposition)
Gourieroux, Laurent & Scaillet 2000 (J. Empirical Finance 7:225, Euler decomposition of VaR)
Rockafellar & Uryasev 2000 (J. of Risk 2:21, CVaR/Expected Shortfall)

cards.method: Skew-t fit to fitted quantiles (ABG Growth-at-Risk «step 2») + density/ES
cards.when: you have conditional quantiles (from #64 GaR) and you want the FULL growth density: quantile matching to a skew-t (Adrian-Boyarchenko-Giannone 2019) -> density/CDF + expected shortfall / downside risk
cards.when_not: you only want the quantiles (stop at #64); you have a raw sample of returns (VaR/ES directly -> #65); you want an MLE skew-t regression on raw data (selm, outside the surface); non-monotone probs (crossing) -> fix that first

alternatives.criterion: you do not need the full density/ES, only the GaR/upside points
you have a raw sample of returns (not conditional quantiles) -> historical/Gaussian/modified VaR
you want a full ML skew-t regression, not quantile matching (outside the wrapper)
a small/noisy quantile set -> lock nu (e.g. 5) for stability

output_key_fields: dp: c(xi=location, omega=scale, alpha=slant, nu=df) — the fitted skew-t parameters
objective/rmse: weighted SSE / rmse of fitted vs target quantiles (small = a good fit)
fitted_quantiles vs target_quantiles: for a visual check of fit quality (chart-data)
st_density: {x, pdf, cdf} grid (chart-ready full density/CDF)
st_shortfall: {var, es, mean, median} — VaR=quantile, es=Expected Shortfall (ABG downside)
convergence: 0 = converged (hard gate: !=0 -> stop)
interpretation_traps: alpha<0 => negative skewness (a heavy left tail) = the ABG «vulnerable growth» case; alpha>0 = right skew
a small nu (->2) => heavy tails => a much more negative ES; nu<=2 is blocked (infinite variance)
quantile CROSSING in the #64 conditional quantiles => non-monotone => gate stop (an invalid distribution) — fix the crossing first
quantile matching != MLE: the fit is to the quantile points, not to raw data; its quality depends on the number of quantiles & their spread
ES = E[X|X<=VaR] (the left tail); the right-side ES is the 'expected longrise' (upper tail)
CONVERGENCE gate: a non-converged optimisation stops (not a silently bad fit, as in #68)
sources: Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone 2019 AER 109(4):1263-1289 (Vulnerable Growth: skew-t on GaR quantiles)
Azzalini & Capitanio 2003 JRSS-B 65(2):367-389 (skew-t distribution)
sn reference manual (qst/dst/pst, direct parametrization)
precondition_tools: c12_distribution_risk/quantile_regression.qr_growth_at_risk (produces the conditional quantiles input -> probs/quantiles)
st_fit_quantiles (the fit; st_density/st_shortfall take the fit object)

cards.method: Extreme Value Theory — GEV block maxima & GP/PP/Gumbel/Exponential threshold exceedances + return levels
cards.when: modelling the TAIL (tail risk) of a series: the size/frequency of extreme events, return levels/return periods (e.g. a 1-in-100 loss), stress thresholds — through the GEV (block maxima) or GP Peaks-Over-Threshold (POT)
cards.when_not: you care about the body of the distribution rather than the tail; a single fixed-quantile VaR or ES suffices (-> #65); a conditional or time-varying tail (GARCH-EVT, or the quantile-regression Growth-at-Risk of #64); non-stationary EVT with covariates (out of scope here)

alternatives.criterion: you want a fast historical/gaussian/Cornish-Fisher VaR/ES without a tail model — NO extrapolation beyond the sample
a conditional tail (Growth-at-Risk) with covariates rather than an unconditional EVT tail
you have the whole series (not only block maxima) -> POT exploits more tail data
only periodic maxima are available (e.g. annual), or there is no clean threshold

output_key_fields: par: a named vector of parameters — GEV/PP {location,scale,shape}; GP {scale,shape}; Gumbel {location,scale}; Exponential {scale}. shape>0 a heavy tail (Frechet); shape<0 bounded (Weibull); shape~0 light (Gumbel)
se/cov_theta: the standard errors and covariance (ML and generalized ML routes); absent for L-moments; nllh/AIC/BIC for model comparison (also absent for L-moments)
threshold/rate/npy/n_exceed: (GP/PP/Exp) the threshold, the exceedance rate, npy=the number of observations per period_basis (it sets the base of the return periods), the number of exceedances
convergence/converged: the optimiser code (0 means ok) and the converged flag (a blank code from the L-moment route counts as ok) — ALWAYS read it, since the node is stateless and stderr is lost
evt_return_level: return_periods + estimate + ci_lower/ci_upper (delta method) — chart-data for a return-level plot
evt_threshold_diag: mrl_* (the mean residual life with its band) and stab_* (the transformed scale and shape with their bands) per threshold — the grids for threshold selection, with NO plot
interpretation_traps: npy trap: for GP/PP, time_units sets npy (the default 'days'->365.25). Wrong time_units => the return levels are interpreted on the WRONG base (e.g. 'annual' on monthly data). Set time_units correctly and read npy from the output

the sign of shape = the tail regime: shape>0 (Frechet, a heavy tail, infinite moments of order>1/shape); shape<0 (Weibull, a bounded upper tail); shape≈0 (Gumbel/exponential). Large |shape| with few exceedances is unstable

threshold bias-variance: too low a threshold -> bias (a non-asymptotic GP); too high -> variance (few exceedances). evt_threshold_diag shows the lowest u above which the mean excess (linear) & shape stabilise

return period > 1: every return period must be > 1 (rlevd); the 100-year level = the 1-1/100 quantile, NOT 'the maximum in 100 years'. The normal-approximation CIs understate the uncertainty far into the tail

the L-moment route is robust but returns NO standard errors, AIC or negative log-likelihood, and covers GEV and GP only. For model comparison or inference use ML or generalized ML; the latter helps when the ML shape estimate is unstable on a small sample
sources: Gilleland & Katz 2016 JSS 72(8) (extreme value analysis)
Coles 2001, An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values (GEV/GP, threshold selection, return levels)
Embrechts, Kluppelberg & Mikosch 1997, Modelling Extremal Events for Insurance and Finance (POT, tail index)
McNeil, Frey & Embrechts 2015, Quantitative Risk Management 2nd ed. §5-7 (EVT VaR/ES, mean excess)
precondition_tools: evt_threshold_diag (POT: choose the threshold BEFORE the GP/PP fit — mean-residual-life linearity + parameter stability)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (check stationarity/approximate iid behaviour: stationary EVT assumes approximately iid exceedances)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a loss/return series from a file)

cards.method: Expectile-based extreme tail risk (extreme/intermediate expectiles + marginal expected shortfall + the heavy-tail index)
cards.when: a heavy-tailed financial series (fat tails, gamma>0); you want coherent tail-risk measures BEYOND the sample — extreme expectiles (asymmetric minimization, coherent), the systemic marginal expected shortfall E[Y|X extreme], or the heavy-tail index gamma with asymptotic CIs
cards.when_not: light-tailed or bounded data (gamma near 0, where the Hill estimator breaks down); a small n (below roughly 100 for an extreme level); a plain in-sample historical or gaussian VaR and ES (-> #65); a quantile-based conditional Growth-at-Risk with covariates (-> #64)

alternatives.criterion: in-sample ES/CVaR (historical/gaussian/Cornish-Fisher) without extrapolation beyond the sample
a conditional downside quantile with covariates (Growth-at-Risk), not an unconditional extreme tail
coherent expectile-based systemic risk rather than the quantile-based QuantMES
the quantile-based indirect estimator when the direct LAWS one is unstable at the extreme level

output_key_fields: er_expectiles: expectile (the point estimate), level (intermediate or extreme), variance + ci_lower/ci_upper (the asymptotic band; absent when the variance is not requested), biasTerm
er_mes: mes (E[series1|series2 extreme]), estimator (quantile/expectile), variance + ci_lower/ci_upper, conf_level
er_tail_index: hill_gamma (the Hill estimate), hill_ci_lower/upper, hill_bias, eb_gamma (the expectile-based estimate; blank when tau was not supplied)
object: the full raw result (HatQMES, gammaHat, ExpctHat and the rest)
interpretation_traps: tau is the INTERMEDIATE level (tau_n->1); tau1 is the EXTREME level; tau1 > tau is required — reversing them -> a silently wrong prediction (the gate blocks it)
MES DIRECTION: MES = E[series1 (data) | series2 (data2) extreme]; data2 is the conditioning/systemic variable (column 2 internally), NOT data
an expectile != a quantile: the expectile minimises an asymmetric squared loss (a coherent risk measure); it is not the tau-quantile
gamma (the tail index) = 1/alpha (Pareto); gamma>=0.5 -> infinite variance, gamma>=1 -> an infinite mean; this is critical for the validity of the measures
k, the intermediate sequence, is a bias-variance tradeoff: a small k gives high variance, a large k gives bias; k>=n or k=0 silently return a blank or a zero (the gate blocks them)
the asym-Dep variance requires bigBlock/smallBlock (big blocks separated by small blocks); without them the variance is blocked by a clean gate instead of a cryptic error
fully deterministic: the CIs are ASYMPTOTIC (closed form), NOT bootstrap — no dependence on a seed
sources: Padoan, S.A. & Stupfler, G. (2022). Joint inference on extreme expectiles for multivariate heavy-tailed distributions. Bernoulli 28(2)
Davison, A.C., Padoan, S.A. & Stupfler, G. (2023). Tail Risk Inference via Expectiles in Heavy-Tailed Time Series. JBES 41(3) 876-889
Daouia, A., Girard, S. & Stupfler, G. (2018). Estimation of tail risk based on extreme expectiles. JRSS-B 80, 263-292
Hill, B.M. (1975). A simple general approach to inference about the tail of a distribution. Annals of Statistics 3, 1163-1174
precondition_tools: er_tail_index (the Hill gamma>0 & its CI: confirm the heavy tail BEFORE the extreme measures; gamma>=0.5 -> infinite variance)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (EVT wants (approximately) stationary data, not trending levels)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a return series from a file)

cards.method: Conditional & unconditional expectiles (Expectiles-at-Risk / a GaR analogue, LAWS)
cards.when: you want least-asymmetrically-weighted-squares expectile curves in the tails of the conditional distribution — an Expectile-at-Risk / GaR analogue sensitive to the MAGNITUDE of the tail; or the unconditional expectile of a vector
cards.when_not: you want a plain quantile or VaR, non-crossing and robust to outliers -> #64; you want a full density forecast or a skew-t -> #95; you want a closed-form ES or CVaR -> #65

alternatives.criterion: you want the quantile/VaR interpretation (P[Y<q]=tau), robustness to outliers, non-crossing
you want a FULL parametric density forecast (skew-t) rather than tail points
the expectile curves cross -> impose monotonicity/no crossing
you want automatic selection of lambda (schall/gcv) rather than a manual lambda

output_key_fields: asymmetries: the expectile levels (asymmetry weights) that were estimated
intercepts: the expectile-specific intercept per level
coefficients: a list per covariate — a matrix [1 x #levels] of the effects per expectile
fitted: an n x #levels matrix with the conditional expectile curves (chart-data)
lambda: the smoothing parameters per term (after schall/gcv/.. or fixed)
expectiles (exr_expectile): one unconditional expectile per prob (0.5 = the arithmetic mean)
interpretation_traps: an expectile ≠ a quantile: the tau-expectile does NOT satisfy P[Y<=e]=tau; it is asymmetric L2 (sensitive to the magnitude of the tail, NOT robust to outliers the way a quantile is)
the 0.5-expectile EQUALS the (conditional) mean, not the median
estimate='laws' does NOT guarantee non-crossing expectile curves; use restricted/bundle/sheets if they cross
smooth='fixed' -> lambda is used as supplied; schall/gcv/ocv select it automatically (the returned lambda then differs from the input)
probs endpoints 0/1 in exr_expectile give the min/max; in the conditional fit the levels must lie strictly in (0,1)
sources: Schnabel & Eilers 2009 CSDA 53:4168 (optimal expectile smoothing, the LAWS algorithm)
Newey & Powell 1987, 'Asymmetric least squares estimation and testing', Econometrica 55:819
Sobotka & Kneib 2012, 'Geoadditive expectile regression', CSDA 56:755 (restricted/bundle/sheets)
Bellini & Di Bernardino 2017, 'Risk management with expectiles', Eur. J. Finance 23:487 (Expectile-at-Risk)
precondition_tools: exr_expectile (the unconditional expectile: an asymmetry benchmark before the conditional fit)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the panel/series data_frame first)
c12_distribution_risk/quantile_regression.qr_growth_at_risk (compare with the GaR quantile before choosing an expectile)

cards.method: Joint (VaR, ES) regression (Fissler-Ziegel) + an ESR-based Expected Shortfall backtest
cards.when: jointly modelling Value-at-Risk & Expected Shortfall as functions of covariates (semiparametric FZ scoring); or evaluating (backtesting) external ES forecasts against realised returns
cards.when_not: a single quantile, VaR only -> #64; an unconditional VaR or ES from history or a gaussian -> #65; a coverage-only VaR backtest (Kupiec, Christoffersen) is not here; you need a full predictive distribution -> #94 or #95

alternatives.criterion: you want only the conditional quantile/VaR (Growth-at-Risk), not the ES jointly
an unconditional ES/CVaR from a return series without covariates
the ES forecasts/estimates are not guaranteed negative (types 1-3 require a negative domain)
you want to test the ES given the VaR (regressing on q & e) rather than a strict ES-only test

output_key_fields: es_joint_reg coefficients: named (bq_0. the VaR equation; be_0. the ES equation); coefficients_q / coefficients_e: the two parts separately
std_errors (es_joint_reg): the asymptotic sandwich standard errors (blank when the covariance failed); loss: the Fissler-Ziegel score at the optimum; nobs
vcov_ok/vcov_note (es_joint_reg): a convergence and degeneracy flag — False means the covariance failed, or gave negative variances, on a small or degenerate sample
es_backtest pvalue_twosided_asymptotic: the main p-value; version 3 adds pvalue_onesided_asymptotic; the pvalue_*_bootstrap fields fill only when B>0
es_all_negative (es_backtest): False means the ES forecasts are not all negative — a possible domain violation for the G2 types 1-3, so the p-value is suspect
interpretation_traps: the backtest H0 = the forecasts are correct; a SMALL p-value => REJECTION (a bad risk model), not the other way round
a singular design matrix in es_backtest: q/e are nearly constant — you need time-varying risk forecasts

blank standard errors from es_joint_reg (vcov_ok=False): the asymptotic sandwich fails on small or degenerate samples -> raise n or check the collinearity, and do NOT read the point estimates as significant
es_all_negative=False: the G2 scoring functions (types 1-3) require negative ES forecasts; positive values silently produce a suspect p-value
version 3 (Strict Intercept) tests whether the ES of the forecast error r-e is zero; version 1 (Strict ESR) regresses the returns on e only; a different hypothesis, they are not interchangeable
the bootstrap p-values are blank when B=0; they are stochastic, so the generator is seeded (2025) for reproducibility
sources: Dimitriadis & Bayer 2019, 'A joint quantile and expected shortfall regression framework' (Electronic J. Statistics 13:1823)
Bayer & Dimitriadis 2022, 'Regression-based expected shortfall backtesting' (J. Financial Econometrics 20:437, doi:10.1093/jjfinec/nbaa013)
Fissler & Ziegel 2016 (Annals of Statistics 44:1680, joint elicitability of VaR & ES)
precondition_tools: es_backtest (post: backtest the VaR/ES forecasts; H0 is correct calibration -> you want a LARGE p-value)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load returns + covariates into a data_frame before es_joint_reg)

cards.method: Quantile Regression Forests (nonparametric conditional quantiles / Growth-at-Risk)
cards.when: non-parametric conditional quantiles y|x with non-linearities/interactions & many predictors; a lower-tail quantile = a nonparametric Growth-at-Risk without imposing a linear form
cards.when_not: you want interpretable coefficients or inference per covariate -> #64; a very small n (the trees overfit and the out-of-bag R² is unreliable); a purely time-series volatility-driven tail -> GARCH; a descriptive tail with no covariates -> #65

alternatives.criterion: you want linear, interpretable coefficients + analytic/bootstrap inference per covariate rather than a black-box forest
you want the FULL growth density + expected shortfall from the fitted quantiles (ABG step 2)
you want honest splitting / treatment heterogeneity together with quantiles
you want a full posterior / non-crossing quantiles / an explicit skew-t likelihood

output_key_fields: qrf_fit: the fitted forest handle; ntree/nodesize/mtry/n/n_predictors/predictors; y_range (min and max)
qrf_fit: rsq_oob/mse_oob, the out-of-bag pseudo-R² and MSE diagnostics; degenerate (True when rsq_oob is blank -> an unreliable fit)
qrf_fit: importance (IncNodePurity per predictor; variable-importance chart-data); seed
qrf_predict: predictions (a matrix n_new x length(quantiles); one column per quantile — chart-data); quantiles; n_new; column labels
interpretation_traps: a categorical y is ACCEPTED at fit time but FAILS at the quantiles (a silent trap) — the wrapper blocks it in qrf_fit
the trees do NOT guarantee non-crossing; with a small n/few trees check the monotonicity of the predictions across quantiles empirically
the seed applies only to qrf_fit (stochastic bootstrap trees); qrf_predict is DETERMINISTIC (aggregating leaf values) — it takes no seed
degenerate=True (a blank out-of-bag R²) means a nearly constant response, or an excessive nodesize -> the quantiles are close to useless
quantiles outside [0,1] are blocked cleanly (the raw routine produced cryptic 'minimal/maximal values' errors)
newdata must contain ALL the predictor columns from training (gate); a single quantile is normalised to a 1-column matrix
sources: Meinshausen (2006) 'Quantile Regression Forests', JMLR 7:983-999
Breiman (2001) Random Forests (Machine Learning 45:5-32; the random-forest engine)
Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone (2019) 'Vulnerable Growth' AER 109:1263-1289 (the GaR context)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the frame of predictors and response; clean the gaps first — the forest does NOT accept them)
qrf_predict (conditional quantiles at new x; the mandatory second link after qrf_fit)
c12_distribution_risk/quantile_regression.qr_growth_at_risk (the parametric linear GaR as a benchmark/cross-check)

cards.method: Parametric distribution fitting (fit/GOF/Cullen-Frey/bootstrap CIs)
cards.when: you have a univariate sample (returns/losses/counts) and you want to fit a parametric distribution, test how well it fits (KS/CvM/AD/chisq), and quantify the parameter uncertainty with a bootstrap
cards.when_not: regression or conditional quantiles (-> #64); explicit tail or EVT extremes (-> #191/#192); a time series with autocorrelation (fit the residuals, not the raw levels); censored data (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: you want a conditional distribution/quantiles as a function of covariates, not an unconditional fit
only the tail matters (block maxima / POT), not the whole distribution
you want a skewed/heavy-tailed closed form fitted to already estimated quantiles
you want to minimise a GOF distance directly (tail-focused) rather than the likelihood

output_key_fields: fd_fit: estimate (the named parameters) + sd (SE from the vcov); aic/bic/loglik for model selection; convergence/converged (0 = OK); distname/method/discrete

fd_goodness_of_fit: ks/cvm/ad (the statistics; blank for discrete distributions); kstest/cvmtest/adtest (a verbal decision, or 'not computed'); aic/bic; chisq/chisqpvalue/chisqdf (the main criterion for discrete distributions)
fd_cullen_frey: skewness/kurtosis + boot_skewness/boot_kurtosis (the Cullen-Frey cloud as chart-data); min/max/median/mean/sd; n
fd_bootstrap_ci: CI (a matrix Median/2.5%/97.5% per parameter); boot_estimates (the full sample, chart-data); n_converged/conv_rate (degeneracy)
interpretation_traps: silently wrong support: nbinom on negative values and pois on non-integers produce SILENTLY false estimates -> explicit gates per distribution (positive>0; beta∈(0,1); counts = non-negative INTEGERS)
AIC/BIC are comparable ONLY across distributions on the SAME data with the same parameter-count penalty; lower = better, not absolute
cvmtest/adtest = 'not computed' for distributions where the p-value is undefined (e.g. norm); this does NOT mean a good fit
for discrete distributions (Poisson, negative binomial) the KS, CvM and AD statistics are blank — judge from chisq and its p-value
the Cullen-Frey bootstrap cloud is stochastic, so the generator is seeded (2025); the reference routine does not return the cloud at all, only a plot — it is reproduced explicitly here
bootstrap CIs assume the correct family; check fd_goodness_of_fit first — a CI under the wrong distribution is misleadingly narrow
sources: Delignette-Muller & Dutang 2015 JSS 64(4) (fitting distributions to data)
Cullen & Frey 1999, 'Probabilistic Techniques in Exposure Assessment' (the Cullen-Frey graph)
Cramer-von Mises / Anderson-Darling GOF (Stephens 1986)
precondition_tools: fd_cullen_frey (before the fit: the Cullen-Frey skewness/kurtosis -> which families are plausible)
fd_goodness_of_fit (after the fit: KS/CvM/AD + AIC/BIC to compare candidate distributions)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the sample from CSV/TSV if needed)

cards.method: Copula dependence + tail dependence + goodness of fit (joint stress)
cards.when: modelling the DEPENDENCE of two (or more) series separately from the marginals; especially tail co-movement (crash/stress) in returns/losses; testing whether the candidate family fits the data
cards.when_not: univariate risk (the VaR/ES of one series -> #65); raw (non-uniform) data without pobs; temporal/dynamic dependence (a GARCH copula is out of scope); dim>2 for the tail index (it is defined only in the bivariate case)

alternatives.criterion: downside/crisis co-movement (lower-tail dependence; losses together)
upside co-movement / boom clustering (upper-tail dependence)
symmetric tail dependence at both ends (heavy joint tails)
dependence without extreme tail co-movement (Gaussian/Frank -> lambda=0)
univariate downside risk of one series, not joint dependence
d>2 with asymmetric pairwise dependences (a regular vine)

output_key_fields: estimate/std_errors (cop_fit): the named copula parameters (Clayton: alpha; Gumbel and Frank: param; normal and t: rho, plus df for the t); the standard errors come from the covariance and are blank when it was not computed, as for the t degrees of freedom
loglik/aic/bic/kendall_tau (cop_fit): the fit diagnostics; kendall_tau is the dependence implied by the fitted copula (blank above two dimensions)
convergence/converged (cop_fit): 0 and True mean the optimiser converged; blank for the inversion-of-tau and inversion-of-rho routes, which do not optimise
lower/upper (cop_tail_index): the coefficients of tail dependence in [0,1] (0 means asymptotic independence in that tail)
statistic/p_value (cop_gof): the Cramér-von Mises Sn plus a parametric-bootstrap p (H0 = the family fits, so a SMALL p is a rejection)
interpretation_traps: GoF polarity: a LARGE p_value is GOOD (the family is not rejected); a small p means the copula does NOT fit — the classic sign-reversal mistake
tailIndex is DEPRECATED -> the wrapper uses lambda (the same lower/upper; it avoids a future breakage)

clayton = the LOWER tail (co-crash); gumbel = the UPPER tail (co-boom); normal & frank give lambda 0 in both tails even when the overall correlation is high (the trap: a high rho does not imply tail dependence)
the input MUST be pseudo-observations in [0,1]^d; fitCopula does NOT check the range (a silently wrong log-likelihood) — the wrapper blocks it with a hard gate; run pobs first
the cop_gof p_value is STOCHASTIC (a parametric bootstrap with N replicates); the seed defaults to 2025 -> reproducible; a small N -> a noisy p
tail_index is bivariate ONLY (dim==2); for dim>2 the function blocks explicitly
sources: Hofert, Kojadinovic, Maechler & Yan 2018, 'Elements of Copula Modeling with the reference' (Springer)
Genest, Remillard & Beaudoin 2009 (Insurance: Math. & Econ. 44:199, the parametric-bootstrap GoF Sn)
Joe 2014, 'Dependence Modeling with Copulas' (CRC) §2 (tail dependence coefficients)
Nelsen 2006, 'An Introduction to Copulas' 2nd ed. (Archimedean families)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the series; then convert them to pseudo-observations with pobs)
cop_fit (fit FIRST; it produces the fitCopula handle for tail_index/gof)
cop_gof (post: a parametric-bootstrap GoF; a large p means the family is not rejected)

cards.method: Regular-vine copulas — a pair-copula construction of the joint dependence (structure selection + loglik + simulate)
cards.when: multivariate (d>=2) dependence with tail dependence/asymmetry beyond linear correlation; the input is pseudo-observations with uniform [0,1] margins (PIT/rank); you want a flexible joint model + scenario simulation
cards.when_not: linear correlation/Gaussian dependence suffices (use the covariance); raw returns without a margin transform (apply PIT/pobs first); temporal dependence/volatility (06-volatility); d=1

alternatives.criterion: symmetric dependence suffices; the pair-copula flexibility is not needed
univariate/bivariate tail risk without a full vine
portfolio risk decomposition under linear assumptions
there is one dominant variable driving the whole dependence (a star structure)

output_key_fields: Matrix: the lower-triangular structure matrix of the vine (which pairs sit in each tree)
family / family_names: the pair-copula codes & names per position (0 = independence)
par / par2: the parameters of each pair copula (par2 only for t/two-parameter families)
tau: the implied Kendall's tau per pair; log_lik / AIC / BIC: the fit-time goodness
all_independence: True when EVERY family is 0 (a degenerate, independent vine)
vine_loglik: loglik (a scalar or per observation), AIC, BIC, npars on NEW data
vine_sim: sim = an NxD matrix of simulated pseudo-observations in [0,1] (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: the input MUST be pseudo-observations in [0,1] (a PIT or rank transform), NOT raw returns; gaps are blocked explicitly, since the raw routine silently falls back to pairwise-complete data
a family of 0 at a position means an independence copula there; all_independence=True means the vine found no dependence at all
the par values are interpreted PER family (a Clayton theta != a Gumbel theta != a Frank one); read family_names alongside par
the AIC/BIC from vine_loglik are computed on the SUPPLIED data (for a holdout comparison); the fit-time AIC/BIC from vine_select are on the training set
vine_sim is STOCHASTIC -> the same seed => identical output (default 2025); the output is in copula space [0,1], an inverse margin transform is needed for return space
CVine vs RVine: a CVine imposes a star structure per tree (less flexible); the default is RVine (the Dissmann greedy MST)
sources: Aas, Czado, Frigessi & Bakken 2009, 'Pair-copula constructions of multiple dependence', Insurance: Math. & Econ. 44:182-198
Dissmann, Brechmann, Czado & Kurowicka 2013, 'Selecting and estimating regular vine copulae', CSDA 59:52-69 (the RVineStructureSelect algorithm)
Czado 2019, Analyzing Dependent Data with Vine Copulas (Springer Lecture Notes in Statistics)
precondition_tools: vine_loglik (in-sample vs holdout loglik: is the structure over-fitted?)
vine_sim (a posterior-predictive check: simulated vs empirical dependence)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the pseudo-observations)

cards.method: SDE scenario generation (short-rate/asset diffusion paths) + a martingale no-arbitrage check
cards.when: generating stochastic scenarios (Monte Carlo paths) for a short rate (Vasicek/CIR/OU) or an asset (GBM); stress testing/ESG cash-flow projection; checking the no-arbitrage property of the simulation
cards.when_not: you want to ESTIMATE SDE parameters from data (quasi-ML estimation is out of scope); jump, Lévy or COGARCH dynamics; fitting a distribution to fitted quantiles (-> #95); VaR or ES on historical returns (-> #65)

alternatives.criterion: VaR/ES on HISTORICAL returns, not a forward-looking simulation
a closed-form parametric distribution on fitted quantiles rather than path simulation

alternatives.alt: the jump, Lévy and quasi-ML extensions (not exposed)
alternatives.criterion: jumps, heavy tails, or parameter estimation from data (a future node)

output_key_fields: paths: a NUMERIC matrix (rows=time=n_steps+1, cols=paths) — chart-data; paths[1,]=xinit
time: the grid [0.T] of length n_steps+1; terminal_values: the values at T per path
summary_mean / summary_quantiles: the per-time mean & q5/q25/q50/q75/q95 (fan chart)
feller_ok: for the CIR process only, 2*kappa*theta >= sigma^2 — otherwise blank; a degeneracy flag, not a hard stop
esg_martingale_test: {theoretical_price, empirical_mean, diff, mc_se, within_ci, n_paths}
interpretation_traps: within_ci=True means the simulation is consistent with no arbitrage (the deflated bond matches the closed-form P(0,T)); False points to Euler bias, too few paths, or wrong parameters
vasicek and ou are THE SAME SDE (theta*(mu-x)dt+sigma dW); a different label, identical dynamics
esg_martingale_test is gated to {vasicek,cir}; gbm/ou (asset models) have NO bond price -> a hard stop, not a silent mistake
the CIR process under an Euler scheme can occasionally approach 0; feller_ok=False warns of a possible loss of positivity
the seed defaults to 2025; the same seed => bit-identical paths (node reproducibility)
sources: Brouste et al. 2014, 'The YUIMA Project', JSS 57(4) <https://www.jstatsoft.org/v57/i04/>
Vasicek 1977 (J. Financial Economics 5:177) — the closed-form P(0,T)
Cox, Ingersoll & Ross 1985 (Econometrica 53:385) — the CIR closed-form P(0,T)
It replaces the -archived ESGtoolkit (simdiff + esgmartingaletest)
precondition_tools: esg_simulate_diffusion (run it FIRST; its object output is the input to esg_martingale_test)
esg_martingale_test (a validation gate: E[exp(-∫r)] ≈ the closed-form P(0,T); vasicek/cir only)

cards.method: VaR and ES backtesting: Kupiec, Christoffersen, dynamic quantile and traffic light
cards.when: a risk model produces quantile forecasts, and whether those forecasts were any good is a testable question the regulator will ask
cards.when_not: there are too few exceedances for any test to have power -- at 99% on one year of daily data you expect two or three

alternatives.criterion: does the exceedance rate match
are exceedances also independent over time
regression-based, or for expected shortfall

output_key_fields: exceedances: count and rate against the expected
kupiec, christoffersen, dq: the test statistics and p-values
independence: whether exceedances cluster
traffic_light: the supervisory zone
interpretation_traps: CLUSTERED EXCEEDANCES ARE THE REAL FAILURE: a model can hit its unconditional rate exactly while concentrating every breach in one week, which Kupiec alone cannot detect
expected shortfall is not elicitable on its own, which is why its backtests are constructed differently and are less powerful
with a one-year window at 99% the tests have almost no power; a pass is very weak evidence
sources: Kupiec 1995 (Journal of Derivatives 3:73-84)
Christoffersen 1998 (International Economic Review 39:841)
Acerbi & Szekely 2014 (Risk 27:76)

cards.method: CAViaR and filtered historical simulation
cards.when: modelling the quantile directly, or combining a volatility model with the empirical shock distribution, instead of assuming a parametric tail
cards.when_not: the sample is too short to estimate a quantile model; you need the whole density rather than one quantile

alternatives.criterion: you accept a distributional assumption
the quantile has its own dynamics
you want a volatility model plus an empirical tail

output_key_fields: var_forecast: the quantile forecast path
params: quantile-model parameters, where CAViaR is used
standardised_residuals: the empirical distribution used by filtered simulation
hit_sequence: exceedance indicators for backtesting
interpretation_traps: FILTERED HISTORICAL SIMULATION CANNOT PRODUCE A LOSS LARGER THAN THE WORST STANDARDISED SHOCK SEEN, scaled by current volatility -- its tail is bounded by history
CAViaR is estimated by non-smooth optimisation with many local optima; multiple starting values are required
the quantile model gives no expected shortfall directly, since it models one quantile rather than the tail
sources: Engle & Manganelli 2004 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 22:367-381)
Barone-Adesi, Giannopoulos & Vosper 1999 (Journal of Futures Markets 19:583)

cards.method: Extreme value workflow: threshold selection, mean residual life and return levels
cards.when: the question is about the tail beyond what the sample contains, where no empirical or kernel method can help
cards.when_not: the quantile of interest is well inside the data; the sample has too few exceedances above any credible threshold

alternatives.criterion: you have enough exceedances and want efficiency
the data are naturally blocked
the quantile is inside the data

output_key_fields: params: generalised Pareto or generalised extreme value parameters
threshold: the selected threshold and the diagnostics behind it
return_levels: levels for the requested return periods, with intervals
shape: the tail index, which determines whether moments exist
interpretation_traps: THE THRESHOLD CHOICE DOMINATES EVERYTHING: too low breaks the asymptotic justification, too high leaves no data, and the estimates move a great deal between them
a shape parameter above 0.5 means the variance is infinite and above 1 the mean is infinite -- report it, because it changes what statistics are even defined
return-level confidence intervals from the delta method are badly asymmetric in the tail; profile likelihood is the honest choice
sources: Coles 2001, An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values
Davison & Smith 1990 (JRSS-B 52:393-442)
pyextremes

cards.method: L-moments and regional frequency analysis
cards.when: estimating distribution shape robustly in small samples, and pooling across sites to estimate tails no single site can support
cards.when_not: the sites are not homogeneous, where pooling imports bias; conventional moments are adequate

alternatives.criterion: large sample, no outliers
small sample or heavy tails
many similar sites, each with short records

output_key_fields: l_moments: the sample L-moments and their ratios
fitted: distribution parameters estimated from them
homogeneity: test that sites can be pooled -- the assumption regionalisation rests on
discordancy: sites inconsistent with the region
interpretation_traps: POOLING HETEROGENEOUS SITES IMPORTS BIAS into every site's estimate; the homogeneity test is the precondition, not a formality
L-moments are far more robust than conventional moments to outliers, which is exactly why they are used for tails
the regional growth curve assumes a common shape with site-specific scale, and that assumption is what buys the extra precision
sources: Hosking 1990 (JRSS-B 52:105-124)
Hosking & Wallis 1997, Regional Frequency Analysis
lmoments3

cards.method: Distributional regression: location, scale and shape
cards.when: covariates shift not only the mean but the variance, skewness or tail of the outcome distribution
cards.when_not: only the conditional mean matters; the sample is too small to estimate several distributional parameters

alternatives.criterion: only the mean matters
you want quantiles without a distributional family
you want a full parametric conditional distribution

output_key_fields: params: coefficients for each distributional parameter
fitted_distribution: the conditional distribution per observation
quantiles: implied conditional quantiles
diagnostics: randomised quantile residuals, which should be standard normal
interpretation_traps: A COVARIATE CAN SHIFT THE VARIANCE WITHOUT SHIFTING THE MEAN, and a mean regression will report nothing at all -- that is the case this method exists for
the distributional family is an assumption; randomised quantile residuals are how it is checked, and they must be examined
with several distributional parameters the likelihood is often multimodal and starting values matter
sources: Rigby & Stasinopoulos 2005 (Applied Statistics 54:507-554)
Klein, Kneib, Lang & Sohn 2015 (Annals of Applied Statistics 9:1024)

cards.method: Copula goodness of fit, tail dependence and dynamic copulas
cards.when: the dependence structure matters in the tails, where a correlation coefficient says nothing and the wrong copula understates joint extremes
cards.when_not: the margins are the question rather than the dependence; the sample is too small for tail dependence to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: no tail dependence, the common default
tail dependence is present
dependence changes over time

output_key_fields: fitted: the selected copula and its parameters
tail_dependence: lower and upper coefficients
gof: goodness-of-fit statistic and its bootstrap p-value
dynamic_params: time-varying dependence, where fitted
interpretation_traps: THE GAUSSIAN COPULA HAS ZERO TAIL DEPENDENCE BY CONSTRUCTION; using it when joint extremes matter understates them systematically, which is the lesson of 2008
goodness-of-fit tests for copulas need a parametric bootstrap because the margins are estimated; asymptotic p-values are wrong
tail-dependence coefficients are estimated from the joint extremes only, so they rest on very few observations
sources: Joe 2014, Dependence Modeling with Copulas
Patton 2006 (International Economic Review 47:527-556)
Genest, Remillard & Beaudoin 2009 (Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 44:199)
copulae

cards.method: Stress-scenario design: historical, hypothetical and reverse
cards.when: constructing the shocks a portfolio or balance sheet is tested against, in a way that is severe but not arbitrary
cards.when_not: the scenario set is prescribed by a supervisor; the risk factors have no joint history to draw on

alternatives.criterion: replay an actual episode
a stated combination of shocks
start from the loss and find what causes it

output_key_fields: scenarios: the constructed shock vectors
plausibility: Mahalanobis distance of each scenario from the joint distribution
loss: portfolio impact per scenario
reverse_scenario: the most plausible scenario producing a stated loss
interpretation_traps: A SCENARIO CAN BE SEVERE AND IMPOSSIBLE at the same time; the plausibility metric is what separates a stress test from an arbitrary number
historical scenarios embed the correlations of that episode, which may not be the current ones
reverse stress testing finds the MOST PLAUSIBLE path to a given loss, which is a different and usually more useful question than the loss from a given shock
sources: Breuer, Jandacka, Rheinberger & Summer 2009 (International Journal of Central Banking 5:205-224)
Basel Committee 2018, Stress testing principles

cards.method: Option-implied risk-neutral density as a growth-at-risk input
cards.when: market-implied densities carry forward-looking information no historical model has, and can condition a growth-at-risk or fan-chart exercise
cards.when_not: no liquid option market exists for the relevant variable; the risk premium wedge cannot be adjusted for

alternatives.criterion: no option data available

alternatives.alt: option-implied density as a conditioning variable
alternatives.criterion: market information is available
surveys are available and physical rather than risk neutral

output_key_fields: implied_quantiles: option-implied quantiles of the underlying
gar_conditioning: the implied variables fed into the growth-at-risk model
risk_premium_adjustment: the wedge applied, where one is
comparison: implied against historical quantiles
interpretation_traps: OPTION-IMPLIED DENSITIES ARE RISK NEUTRAL, not physical; feeding them into a forecast without adjusting for the risk premium biases the tail systematically
the wedge between risk-neutral and physical densities is itself time varying and largest exactly in stressed periods
the underlying is usually a financial variable, so the link to a macro variable is an additional modelling step with its own error
sources: Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone 2019 (American Economic Review 109:1263-1289)
Ait-Sahalia & Lo 2000 (Journal of Econometrics 94:9)
